description: Fig. 3 is a composite flow diagram (schematic plus two real micrograph panels) that explains the training-free MatSAM pipeline for microstructure recognition. The upper row reads left to right under three printed headings: 'Input', 'MatSAM' and 'Output'. The 'Input' panel is a grey-scale micrograph of equiaxed grains with a dashed box marking a cropped region. The 'MatSAM' block contains two sub-blocks: 'Point prompt', holding the labelled boxes 'ROI points' (red), 'merge' and 'Grid points' (blue), and 'Segment anything model', holding 'Points encoder', 'Image encoder' and 'Mask decoder'; grey arrows carry the prompt embedding and image feature vectors into the decoder. The 'Output' panel is the same field of view rendered as a grain-boundary segmentation in which each grain is filled with a distinct pastel colour and marked with a red seed point, again with a dashed inset. The lower row repeats the dashed region five times: 'Region' (raw grain structure), 'ROI points' (sparse red dots), 'Grid points' (dense blue dots), 'Merged' (red plus blue dots) and 'Boundaries' (black lines on white with red dots), linked by '+' and '≫' symbols. No axes, numeric values or scale bars are printed.

observations.observation: Fig. 3 is a three-stage pipeline labelled 'Input', 'MatSAM' and 'Output', read left to right.
The point-prompt module contains three stacked boxes labelled 'ROI points' (red), 'merge' and 'Grid points' (blue), which feed a merged prompt into the model.

The 'Segment anything model' block is drawn with three components labelled 'Points encoder', 'Image encoder' and 'Mask decoder', with a token sequence from the points encoder and a feature vector from the image encoder both entering the decoder.

The 'Output' panel shows the input field of view as coloured grains (each grain a different pastel fill) with red seed points, i.e. an instance-style grain segmentation rather than a binary boundary image.

The lower row shows five states of the same dashed crop: 'Region', 'ROI points' (red dots), 'Grid points' (blue dots), 'Merged' (both dot sets) and 'Boundaries' (black boundary lines on white), joined by '+' and '≫' symbols.
No axes, tick labels, numeric values, legends or scale bars are printed anywhere in the figure.
The caption states that Fig. 3 is a schematic of MatSAM for training-free microstructure recognition.

The citing text states that MatSAM is implemented on SAM, which was pre-trained on the largest segmentation dataset to date and uses an image encoder, a prompt encoder and a segmentation mask decoder.

The citing text states that MatSAM requires no extra training or human labelling: a raw image is processed by the encoder, a prompt is tokenized, and the learned image feature is combined with the prompt embedding to output masks.
The citing text lists the microstructures extracted as grains, phases, precipitates and cracks; the figure itself only illustrates grain segmentation.

subfigures.description: 'Input': grey-scale micrograph of equiaxed grains with a dashed rectangular region marked for cropping; a red and a blue arrow leave the image toward the prompt module.

'MatSAM': two coupled blocks. 'Point prompt' contains 'ROI points' (red text), 'merge' and 'Grid points' (blue text); 'Segment anything model' contains 'Points encoder', 'Image encoder' and 'Mask decoder'. Arrows show a prompt token sequence and an image feature vector feeding the Mask decoder, and a curved red arrow returning to the Output panel.
'Output': segmented version of the input field of view; every grain is filled with a different pastel colour and carries a red dot, overlaid with the corresponding dashed inset.
'Region': the dashed crop shown at higher magnification as a raw grey-scale grain structure with visible boundaries.
'ROI points': same crop with sparse red dots placed on selected grain interiors/boundaries.
'Grid points': same crop with a dense uniform array of blue dots.
'Merged': same crop with the red ROI dots and the blue grid dots combined, preceded by a '+' symbol.
'Boundaries': final binary-style result of the same crop — black grain-boundary lines on a white background with red dots retained, introduced by a '≫' symbol.
